attacks.claim: The launch flips flags for all cardholders at once, with no percentage or cohort stage after the staff pilot, and no go/no-go or abort thresholds for delivery rate, STOP rate, or locker errors before the 10:00 announcement.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 9 09:00: flags on for all cardholders; announcement goes out at 10:00 only after a smoke test of one live text and one locker pickup per branch."

attacks.claim: Lockers are 24/7, but outage alerts page the branch manager and vendor, and the vendor's SLA is 4 hours on-site. No overnight responder is named, so an outage during closed hours has no defined owner.
attacks.evidence: "any locker bank offline > 10 min (pages branch manager + vendor; vendor SLA 4 h on-site)"

attacks.claim: Alerting covers only SMS delivery and webhook failures. Failures in the email or automated phone fallback, which carries "no alert is lost", are not monitored, so a double failure goes unpaged.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: alert for fallback-channel (email or phone call) failure. Stated alerts: "delivery failures > 5% for 15 min, webhook signature failures > 0, any locker bank offline > 10 min"

attacks.claim: The automated phone-call fallback has per-call cost that is outside the $460/month SMS forecast and the $900 cap math. A cap-triggered switch can shift spend to an unbudgeted line.
attacks.evidence: "falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call, which stays on file)" versus "Forecast 38,000 texts/month at about $0.012 all-in = ~$460/month"

attacks.claim: Batching puts one locker code on a message covering two holds, but codes are described as single-use and tied to a cell. The artifact does not say how a batch spanning different pickup locations (locker and desk) or multiple codes is rendered, so at least one hold may be unopenable from the text.
attacks.evidence: "Max 3 texts per patron per day; extra holds are batched into one message." and "2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14."

attacks.claim: The locker_pickup rollback remaps holds and notifies patrons, but it does not say whether codes already sent for locker pickups are invalidated. A live code could still open a cell on hardware that stays powered, or a patron could be left with a code that no longer works.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: code invalidation on locker_pickup off. Artifact states "Codes are single-use, expire at the pickup deadline" and "patrons are notified of the new location"

attacks.claim: The approved 10:00 announcement says text alerts are "for every cardholder", but juvenile cards do not get the SMS option. This fixed copy goes to all patrons and misstates eligibility to guardians and juvenile cardholders.
attacks.evidence: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder." versus "juvenile cards do not show it"

attacks.claim: The SMS flow is promised in Spanish, but only the English disclosure text is shown. Spanish consent wording and whether LGL-118 covered it are not evidenced.
attacks.evidence: "English and Spanish, following the patron's existing language preference." versus the disclosure shown only in English, and "legal review complete (ticket LGL-118)"

attacks.claim: The automated phone-call fallback vendor is not named, and the DPA is cited only for the SMS provider. A separate processor receiving patron phone numbers and notice content has no stated data-processing coverage, and the "no alert is lost" guarantee depends on it.
attacks.evidence: "The SMS provider is covered by our existing DPA (signed 2025-03)" and "automated phone call, which stays on file"

attacks.claim: Retention of the phone number and consent record is undefined while SMS is live. On permanent withdrawal, consent evidence is deleted within 30 days with no dispute or legal-hold carve-out, so the library may be unable to prove consent in a later complaint.
attacks.evidence: "Phone number and consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version) are stored in the patron record" and "If SMS is withdrawn permanently, numbers and consent records are deleted within 30 days"

attacks.claim: The public locker kiosk is described with high-contrast mode, audio guidance, and adjustable text, but the QA table records no assistive-technology test of the kiosk. Only the web opt-in form was tested with screen readers.
attacks.evidence: "screen has high-contrast mode, audio guidance through a headphone jack, and adjustable text size" versus "Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS; 320/768/1280 px layouts | Pass"

attacks.claim: The 38,000 texts/month forecast is not derived from holds volume or opt-in rate. The $900 cap corresponds to about 75,000 texts/month, so adoption growth could hit the cap and silently move all opted-in patrons to fallback channels.
attacks.evidence: "Forecast 38,000 texts/month at about $0.012 all-in = ~$460/month" and "Provider account hard spend cap $900/month, alert to ops at 70%."

attacks.claim: Queued texts release at 08:00 with no stated provider throughput, per-second send rate, or drain-time target. Queue depth is monitored, but no action is defined if it grows.
attacks.evidence: "anything later is queued to 08:00" and "queue depth" appears only as a dashboard metric

attacks.claim: Cap behaviour was tested only with a $5 test cap in test mode. The production $900 cap and the 70% ops alert have no QA evidence at production volume.
attacks.evidence: "Spend cap reached (test cap $5) → fallback to email / phone call | Pass"

attacks.claim: The locker rollback SQL was tested on 1,200 staging rows. Production active-hold count, staff labour to move items to the holds shelf, and the patron notification workload at three branches are not sized.
attacks.evidence: "scripts/remap_locker_holds.sql (tested in staging on 1,200 rows), staff move items to the holds shelf"

attacks.claim: The pickup deadline is shown as a fixed date with no time of day or timezone, and the rule for computing it (per hold, or including the 3-day extension) is not stated.
attacks.evidence: "Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14." and "hold deadlines extend 3 days"

attacks.claim: Card number plus PIN is entered on a public touchscreen. TLS between kiosk and ILS, PIN logging, and shoulder-surfing mitigation are not stated.
attacks.evidence: "or enters card number + PIN, existing ILS PIN lockout applies"

attacks.claim: Lockout is per cell (5 attempts) across 144 cells, with no stated global or per-card throttle, and the code-generation method is not described.
attacks.evidence: "Codes are single-use, expire at the pickup deadline, and 5 wrong attempts lock the cell and alert branch staff."

attacks.claim: Carrier and 10DLC passes were run in test mode on the production provider account, which may not reflect real carrier filtering. The one-week, 64-card staff pilot cannot support the 38k/month forecast or the 5% failure threshold.
attacks.evidence: "Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds) | 0 misdelivered texts" and "against the production SMS provider account in test mode"

attacks.claim: The disclosure says "Msg frequency varies" but does not state the 3-per-day cap the flow enforces.
attacks.evidence: "Msg frequency varies. Msg & data rates may apply." versus "Max 3 texts per patron per day"

attacks.claim: Provider message logs held for 30 days include pickup codes, phone numbers, and branch names. The privacy-policy update lists SMS but does not describe this third-party retention.
attacks.evidence: "it retains message logs 30 days and is barred from marketing use" and "Privacy policy section 4 updated to list SMS"
